item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
• Add Camera: picking a different camera on your network clears the account, name, stream and test result of the one before, so Save stays off until the new camera connects
  • CamDock shows in the Dock by default (turn it off in Settings › General › Show in Dock)
  • CamDock opens the Monitor at launch by default instead of Quick View (turn it off in Settings › General › Open Monitor at launch)
  • Floating Camera: right-click › Open in Monitor stops floating and shows that camera in the Monitor
  • Settings: recordings have their own tab — what's recording now, saved clips and free space, which cameras record, storage and how clips are made
  • Welcome screen shows the CamDock icon
  • Recordings timeline: a video no longer goes black when the playhead moves (while playing) to a moment with fewer cameras
  • Monitor: going between the grid and a single camera (double-click) no longer leaves a camera's video zoomed into a corner of the picture; in a single camera, double-click always goes back to the grid, even while the HD stream is still loading; opening the Monitor brings it back from the Dock if it was minimized
  • Monitor sidebar button moved to the far left of the title bar, above the sidebar; with the sidebar hidden, point at the window's left edge for a "Show sidebar" tab
  • "Hide from screen recording" is now on by default (SPEC D17): CamDock's windows stay out of screen shares, recordings and screenshots unless you turn it off in Settings. A setting you already changed is kept
  • Recordings: open from the menu bar, the Monitor toolbar or sidebar. Browse every clip as a Gallery, a List or a Timeline (⌘1/⌘2/⌘3); search, filter by date, camera and kind, sort; step through results while playing; move clips to the Trash; List column headers sort; dates are picked on a calendar
  • Recordings timeline: a day's clips per camera on a timeline; drag the playhead and every camera that recorded that moment plays side by side; today ends a few minutes after now; each kind has its own colour; camera and kind filters are checklists with search (the Timeline drops the date and sort filters, it has its own day picker); dragging the playhead near a clip snaps to its start (hold Option to scrub freely); up to 6 camera rows show, more scroll up and down; a scroll handle (the whole day with a mark per clip) appears on hover; a legend of kind colours filters by kind; the playhead shows the time in a red pill, round dock buttons and a zoom-span pill (Screendrop-style); layouts for the videos (Automatic, All Cameras, fixed or custom grids with a cell per camera); pick the day on a calendar; right-click a video or a clip for Open, Show in Finder, Move to Trash
  • Get Pro window: Free vs Pro comparison, launch price $19 (regular $29 struck through), Enter License Key
  • Settings → Cameras: "Detect" is now "Kinds of detection", with a note on what it does (alerts, the notch, clips), that it uses each camera's own detection, and that auto-tracking is set in the camera's app
  • Saved PTZ positions (presets, the Go to Camera Preset shortcut) are now part of Pro; pan, tilt and zoom stay free. On Free the presets show dimmed with a lock and open Get Pro
  • Monitor sidebar: CamDock's logo, version and plan (Pro, trial days left, or Free → Upgrade) at the top, and a Get Pro card at the bottom on Free; the Online / Today tiles are replaced by notices floating at the bottom that appear only when something needs a look (a camera offline, disk almost full, alerts paused, quiet hours), each with one action
  • Monitor layouts: All Cameras (every camera on one page), more fixed grids (4 × 3, 4 × 4) and Custom… (any columns × rows up to 6 × 6)
  • Camera offline notifications: hear when a camera has been unreachable for about 2 minutes, and when it's back
  • Quiet hours per detection rule: no notifications and no notch at set times; detections are still recorded
  • Add Camera: pick your camera brand and type its IP to fill the stream addresses; Test connection now says which step failed (reaching the camera, signing in, or getting the picture)
  • Stream Info: right-click a video to see its resolution, codec, frame rate and bitrate
  • Export and import settings: move cameras, rules and settings to another Mac with a .camdock file (camera passwords only with a password you choose)
  • Shortcuts actions: Show Camera, Take Snapshot, Go to Camera Preset, Pause / Resume Detection Alerts, Open Monitor; Pause Alerts for 1 Hour in the menu bar
  • The display stays awake while a camera is in Fullscreen (setting)
  • 7-day Pro trial from the first launch, then CamDock Free (one camera; your other cameras stay saved and locked) — no lockout. One-time Pro license: $29
  • Snapshots: Take Snapshot in a Floating Camera, the Monitor's Single view and Fullscreen saves the picture at full stream resolution to ~/Pictures/CamDock; click the confirmation to show it in Finder
  • Pro: record detections — turn on "Record clips" for All Cameras or one camera; each detection saves a video-only clip (MP4 in ~/Movies/CamDock, kept 7 days by default). Click an activity row in the Monitor sidebar to play it
  • Welcome screen updated: what Quick View, Monitor and Floating Camera do, the Pro trial, and the Local Network permission that comes next
  • Cameras locked on Free no longer send detections or open the notch
  • The notch opens by itself on the camera that detects a person, pet or vehicle, and closes about 8 s after the activity ends (countdown ring; hover to keep it)
  • New minimal idle notch: beside a MacBook's notch a still of the last camera with activity, plus the camera count and a status dot (red during a detection); a small capsule on other displays. On by default
  • Quick View redesigned, compact: videos only in an automatic grid (up to 3×2) with a small floating toolbar; opens and closes with a smooth spring like a real notch; detecting cameras pulse red in the Monitor and the expanded notch
  • Notch display: shows on one display — Automatic (a MacBook display with a notch, else the main one) or one you pick, also from right-click → Show On; no more hopping between monitors. On a MacBook the open notch sits below the camera housing
  • Monitor dashboard: a sidebar with cameras online, detections today, each camera's status and last detection, and today's activity — click a camera to view it alone (⌃⌘S hides it)
  • Detection settings per camera: All Cameras sets the defaults, and any camera can have its own (notify, open the notch, which kinds); kinds a camera doesn't report are dimmed
  • Settings reorganised like System Settings: General, Notch, Cameras (All Cameras + one page per camera), License, About
  • Quick View layout setting: side rail (default), no header, or slim header
  • Double-click a camera in the notch to float it large right under the notch; a focused Floating Camera shows a white ring and Esc closes it
  • Removed: the Notch / Pill shape setting and "Live pill" (the idle notch no longer plays video)
  • New surface model: Quick View (notch) ⇄ Monitor window ⇄ Floating Camera ⇄ Fullscreen
  • Monitor: native window and toolbar, Grid / Single, layouts, Keep on Top, right-click actions; replaces window mode
  • Floating Camera: one camera per window, no prev/next cycling; reopened at launch
  • Open Monitor at launch (replaces "Open in"), Eco mode (substream everywhere)
  • Auto-reconnect with backoff, Retry now, immediate retry on wake / network return
  • Fixed a crash when resizing a Floating Camera by its corner
  • Launch at login now works
  • Copy Diagnostics and persistent logs for bug reports
  • Requires macOS 14 on Apple Silicon
  • Quick View hangs from the top of the screen like a notch again (it was pushed below the menu bar); a Pill shape floats just below the menu bar instead — switch from its right-click menu
  • Quick View shows a page of cameras at a time (1–6 per page, default 3) with ‹ › to the others
  • Monitor: one View menu (Single Camera, Automatic, fixed layouts with pictures) replaces the Grid/Single buttons; cameras that don't fit a layout are on further pages (‹ ›, ⌘← ⌘→), instead of being hidden
  • Fixed: Fullscreen in HD on a 2K camera lost its header and corner controls (name, SD/HD chip, pan & tilt) off the screen edges — the video took the stream's pixel size instead of the space available; hover is also detected when a view opens under the pointer
  • Fixed: picking a camera in Quick View no longer makes every video blink
  • Fixed: the expanded notch no longer collapses when the pointer moves over its top (the menu bar strip)
  • Quick View (notch / pill) is shown only when you turn it on (menu bar, Monitor toolbar or Settings); closing the Monitor no longer brings it up. With both open, videos play in the Monitor and Quick View shows "In Monitor"; a Floating Camera always has its video
  • Clicking the menu bar icon brings the Monitor to the current Space and in front (or opens Quick View); right-click for the menu. The hotkey no longer hides a Monitor left on another Space
  • Menu bar menu follows what's on screen: Open / Close Monitor, Hide / Show Quick View (the old Show / Hide did the same as Open Monitor while the Monitor was open)
  • Floating Camera right-click menu: Stop Floating, Fullscreen, Mute, Keep on Top, Size, Lock Aspect Ratio, Settings, Quit (no more Quick View items)
  • App icon: a blue camera lens (was the generic placeholder)
  • Monitor right-click: Edit Camera… and Remove Camera… (asks first)
  • Only one CamDock runs at a time: opening a second copy brings the running one forward and quits (copies shared settings and cameras but played them twice)
  • Fullscreen zoom up to 400%: zoom bar left of the title, ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0, pinch on the trackpad (zooms at the pointer); drag or two-finger scroll to move around
  • Double-click a Floating Camera for Fullscreen (double-click again or Esc to leave); Fullscreen has a right-click menu (Exit Fullscreen, Mute, Pan & Tilt, Settings, Quit)
  • A new Floating Camera opens at the Medium size (344 pt wide)
  • Drag a video onto another camera in the Monitor or Quick View to change the camera order
  • Drag a video out of the Monitor or Quick View to float it where you drop it (hand cursor, hover hint and tooltip show which videos can be dragged)
  • Fixed: a PTZ preset move no longer stops halfway when the pointer leaves the video or CamDock loses focus
  • Edit a camera's URL, username, password and substream in Settings › Cameras (no more delete and re-add)
  • A lost stream shows the camera's last frame blurred behind "Reconnecting…" / "Couldn't connect" in every view, instead of black or a frozen picture
  • A stream waiting to reconnect tries again as soon as its camera is reachable, instead of waiting out the backoff
  • Detection notifications carry the frame from the moment of the detection (cameras on screen), never an older one
  • Add Camera explains how to allow Local Network access when macOS blocks the scan
  • Cmd+W closes the Monitor, Settings and Add Camera windows; VoiceOver labels for Retry, Add Camera and the Monitor's audio button
